fields.title: Nothing scans the package kac ships

sections.What we are doing instead: The package is built by the publish workflow from the commit on `main`, on a runner GitHub gives fresh for that run. Dependabot watches the dependencies, and [std-CONFIG] requires each pin to name one version. Nothing scans what the build produced before it is pushed.
sections.Why we need it: A scan needs a scanner chosen and a failure path decided, and neither has been done. The package is a documentation tool built from a public repository, by one workflow anybody can read.
sections.What the risk is: Something malicious gets into the package through a dependency or a build step, and nothing looks for it before it ships. A consumer installing `kac` takes what it contains on trust.
sections.What compensates:
* The package is built by one workflow, whose run log is public and records the commit it built.
* [ctl-0007] packs the tool and installs it on every pull request. That copy runs `kac new` and validates the corpus
  it created, so what ships has been run.
* Trusted publishing means no key exists that would let anybody else push under this name.
* nuget.org refuses a second push to a version it already has, so what shipped cannot be replaced.
sections.How it closes: A scan runs over the package and the plugin before they are published, and fails the job on a finding. This record closes when that scan is in the publish workflows.
sections.Scope: The `kac` package on nuget.org, and the plugin served from the marketplace branch.
